analysis.title: Weekly HF Highlights: US L/S Net Lev Declines 8% WoW; HF De-Grossing Persists
key_insights: US L/S net leverage fell 5% on Thursday (Nov 5) alone to 42%, the 5th largest single-day decline on record since 2010. Nets are about 8% lower WoW and at the lowest level of the year, still above the roughly 35% low of April 2025.
US L/S gross leverage ended at 202% and continues to push toward 12-month troughs. Gross is down 4% WoW.

Midterms cleared a political overhang but did not lead to re-risking. HFs used Wednesday's relief rally to keep de-grossing both sides of the portfolio, and the selling continued into a broader long-side supply event on Thursday.

L/S gross flow over the past few months amounts to -10.7% of global GMV at the end of June. Positioning imbalances across most sectors, factors and themes are now moderate, and HFs no longer appear to be driving sharp equity reversals.
AI themes (Hyperscalers, Tech Beneficiaries, Power) are about 32% of total US net exposure, down from 47% at the June peak. HFs are about 2% underweight these names relative to market cap weight.

HFs spent the trailing 4 weeks covering shorts and softening underweights in the areas that rallied most, while cutting longs in the areas that sold off most. Positioning was lighter in the themes that moved most between Wednesday and Thursday.

The average US-based L/S fund lost 72bps in the first days of November, with Thursday at -1.6%. The group took less than 30% of the S&P's losses. YTD the average US L/S fund is +5.7%, and about 35-40% of the cohort is flat to negative YTD.

HF positioning is not extreme enough to trigger a sharp equity move, but HFs can accelerate moves either way. They can sell quickly into further weakness and could be very supportive of a rally given the light positioning.
US L/S net leverage is in the bottom decile of the last decade, which has historically preceded more positive forward S&P returns.

APAC saw de-grossing in well-owned AI trades in Taiwan, South Korea and Hong Kong. Japan saw gross reductions concentrated in Tech, with a smaller share of long capital rotated into Discretionary and Financials.
EU HFs unwound longs in Tech, Energy and Health Care and covered shorts in Consumer. EU remains the smallest share of global gross exposure versus 15-year history.
Asia-based L/S funds are up 4.4% YTD versus MSCI Asia +14.5%. EU-based L/S funds are up 1.5% YTD versus SXXP +13.9%.
Top 50 crowded longs lost 7.49% on Nov 5 versus -5.95% for the top 50 shorts and -4.36% for the S&P 500 TR. Longs-minus-shorts spread is -3.25% WTD and MTD, +11.27% YTD.

sector_views.rationale: HFs cut AI-related longs in the US, Taiwan, South Korea, Hong Kong and Japan, and unwound EU Tech longs. US AI exposure is about 2% underweight versus market cap weight.
EU HFs covered Consumer shorts. In Japan a smaller share of long capital rotated into Discretionary.
Japan HFs rotated a smaller share of long capital into Financials.
EU HFs unwound Health Care longs.

macro_indicators.interpretation: The result did not lead HFs to re-risk. They used the Wednesday relief rally to de-gross.

risk_factors: HFs are sensitive to additional losses and can sell quickly into further weakness.
About 35-40% of US L/S funds are flat to negative YTD.
A long-side supply event on Thursday extended the de-grossing.
